desc:
The avalanche pattern includes many perilous variations. However, there are a couple of simple continuations that Black can choose.

Black has the initial choice of joseki with this pattern. The outcome is typically Black gets the corner and out on the side, White thickness.

Note that this move may be joseki only when White occupies D4, as a ladder from certain avalanche positions (e.g., <position:27044>) won't work otherwise and makes the outcome a bit better for Black. A White stone at C4 is insufficient. See [Michael Redmond, *AlphaGo vs. The World: Game 26, Yun Chanhee 6p (W) vs. AlphaGo Master (B)*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1w1Kx2n44tU&t=182s).
